records.timing: after the first BA number (dev contrast), before gate 1 and holdout-open
records.what: otto_model.check_ba_frame (the check that B enters BA whole, §5.2) runs over chunks of BA_CHECK_CHUNK = 100 000 sessions and sums the counts, instead of one pass over every session
records.why: evaluate holdout BA2026 on the F4 evaluation population (1 000 000 sessions, BA frame 115 M rows) failed with DuckDB OutOfMemoryException (18.6 GiB of the 20 GB memory_limit) inside check_ba_frame: one EXCEPT over every B row of the population. Dry run outside the contract with chunks of 200 000 (code check off, scratch output removed): completed in 390 s, peak RSS 20.2 GB, b_keys_missing 0, b_values_differ 0; the chunk is halved for F5 (~150 rows per session).
records.effect: none on metrics or outputs: every session lies in one chunk, so the summed set counts equal the single pass (test_ba_frame_check_runs_by_chunks_and_counts_every_chunk); agent SQL, columns, parameters, populations and models do not change
records.failed_output: artifacts/otto/fits/holdout-BA2026/eval (status failed); fresh_output moves it to eval.failed-<stamp> on the rerun
records.contract: §7: after the first BA number only technical fixes recorded here; §12 «Память»: a DuckDB memory failure is fixed by a smaller batch — here a batch over sessions is introduced into the check, its comparison logic is unchanged
